blocks.markdown: **Sec. 9(b)(1)** sets the **general deadlines**, subject to **periods otherwise provided by law** and lawful extension rules. The syllabus indicates extensions and definitions, so know the **statutory ground, maximum extension and notice requirements** from the current text. The practical start point is **receipt of the complete application with required documents and payment**; compute **working days, not calendar days**, and check **holidays and agency-specific statutory periods**.

blocks.markdown: Action on applications: approval, denial and deemed approval

**Approval and automatic approval / extension — Sec. 10.** RA 11032 contains an **automatic-approval mechanism** for covered applications where the office **fails to act within the prescribed period**, provided the statutory conditions (**including complete submissions and required fees**) are met. It also has an **automatic-extension concept for qualifying renewals** in the circumstances specified by the Act. The rule is **not “every government silence means approval”**; first establish **coverage, completeness, deadline expiration, the kind of application, and statutory exceptions or procedures**.

**Denial and required notice.** An adverse action should be the kind of **written, reasoned approval or disapproval recognized by Sec. 4(a)**, **communicated within the period** and under Sec. 9. For an exam, distinguish an **actual written denial from inaction**; identify whether **reasons, signer or authority, and appeal or review information** are required by the applicable provision. A **vague oral discouragement** should not be equated automatically with a valid statutory denial.

**Application checklist:**

- Create a **timeline**: submission date; completion or deficiency notice; payment; prescribed deadline; any **lawful extension and notice**; actual action (if any).
- Ask whether the request seeks a **permit, license, clearance, certificate, renewal or another covered service**.
- Before asserting deemed approval, check whether **special law expressly controls**, whether **all documents and fees were submitted**, and what **proof of application or receipt** is available.
- A legal claim **based on deemed approval** is different from a claim for **delay**, an **administrative complaint**, or a **criminal or administrative violation**.
**A processing deadline is not calendar days counted from the first incomplete submission.** Count working days from the complete filing.
**Automatic approval is not a universal rule** that every silent government office approves anything. Deemed approval needs coverage, completeness, deadline expiry, and no controlling exception.

**Simple, complex and highly technical are statutory definitions, not labels chosen to extend time.** Classify under Sec. 4 before applying the deadline. (The definitions live in the policy-and-charter lesson.)

**Check before exam.** When using RA 11032, **verify current implementing rules and agency-specific laws**. The general **3/7/20 working-day standards and automatic-approval provisions** must be applied only after **classifying the transaction and confirming that all statutory predicates are met**.
